request:
to the classify tab, add functionality to find people in the images. load a small, on-premise, efficient model for that. consider that we'll tag some photos to start that classifying good.

moreover, add more categories to the classification - home, restaurant, car, street, nature, work...
notes: Model choice: OpenCV's YuNet (0.2 MB) + SFace (37 MB) onnx from github.com/opencv/opencv_zoo, run by the opencv-python-headless already in requirements (cv2.FaceDetectorYN / FaceRecognizerSF), no new package; ~56 ms a photo at 1024 px. On 40 photos of the 2010 folder: 24 faces, same-person pairs score 0.65-0.81 cosine, 95% of different pairs under 0.35, so MATCH_SIM = 0.40. The tagging is few-shot by design: a name's stored embeddings are the examples and every photo is re-matched on load and after each Save, so a few tags on one folder name the person in all. The new classes are one axis with the old ones (Home, Restaurant, Car, Street, Nature, Work beside Trip, Party, Other photo); the first 30 photos of the 2010 folder came out Work 18 (an office, checked by eye), Home 6, Car 2, Other 2, Restaurant/Nature/Street/Trip 1; event smoothing still pulls only toward Trip/Party. Side effect handled: list_files used to skip any subfolder named like a class, which with Home/Work/Car would have hidden real folders, so the skip is now top-level only. Old cache entries (three score keys, no faces) still load. The scratch test tag (Tester) was removed from people.json afterwards.
work: The Classify tab finds people: a Find people switch adds a face pass (src/faces.py: YuNet + SFace via cv2, downloaded by the same Download Models button) that stores each photo's faces and the names matched; Tag People shows the selected image's faces with a name box each and Save keeps them in people.json and re-matches every loaded photo; a People column, Show filter by person or Unknown faces, People in the sheet; and six new photo classes Home, Restaurant, Car, Street, Nature, Work with CLIP prompts.
